html:
Making a career choice is a long term decision. What is important to know is whether you have it in you what it takes to make a breakthrough in your specific career choice. Out of the many career choices available, medicine has long been the choice of the dedicated & affected.

The various branches of medicine offer a wide range of professional exposure & learning. From the very basic physician which requires MBBS degree to the niche expert surgeon or neurologist, the challenges that the medical field offers is many. What besides these are the questions that one should address while making a career choice of medicine?

Does making a difference to someone’s life aspire you? Taking that step which shall positively affect the health of a person drive you? Troubleshoot the health problems of people, to make their life more comforting, gets you curious. If the answer to most or all these questions is ‘yes’ then probably medicine has made the cut for you.

Still there would surely be more factors to be kept in mind before arriving at such a critical decision. Here, we list a few that shall make your decision making easier:

  • The mention of the abbreviation/title or prefix Dr. before a name is generally considered a matter of pride & honor in the society. Being referred as a doctor gives a sense of achievement & accomplishment to the person. Once on work, it shall certainly instill a sense of confidence & enhance self-esteem.
  • This particular occupation is immune to economic cycles, or any other phase that could prohibit people from going to a doctor. Unlike any other profession, it has an inherent stability that is not susceptible to a downfall as the numerous other career options available.
  • There is a service orientation in medicine. It enables you to be a life-long learner. This particular field of expertise can only expand. Thus, it is essential to be updated with current knowledge & trends in the industry. Such that the practice can be carried out effectively on the person deprived.
  • Quick thinkers have an advantage in this profession, as emergency can strike on anyone. On the spot decision making that can be critical to one’s life is also essential especially let’s say for a surgeon in the operation theatre. People would put their faith in you, & the onus is on you to not let them down.
  • The grades & genres of practice are also varied. One can either practice independently or join a medical institution or hospital. Then one can also become a medical scientist by pursuing medical research. A doctor can become a consultant & open up doors to many health related programs. It can become an adept source of income once the person starts to pick up expertise, find bliss in practice & make a mark in the industry.

Besides these reasons, be prepared for the groundwork that follows once the choice is made. The competition in this field continues to be immense. The courses on offer can also be a hard task to deal with as do the entry exam. It requires discipline and critical thinking is also required. In such a scenario, personal accountability is your best ally.

The sad yet attractive part is that people are increasingly getting negligent of their health, despite the rising consciousness. This is mainly due to time constraints in this fast paced world. There cannot be a dearth in demand, the supply of quality medical professionals should not fall short too.

Frequently asked Questions (FAQ’s):

1. Which are the entrance exams for career in medical?

There are many entrance exams for medical careers, but the most popular ones in India are:

  • NEET (National Eligibility cum Entrance Test): Test): This is the single national-level entrance exam for undergraduate (UG) medical courses in India. It is conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA) and is held once a year. The syllabus for NEET is based on the 11th and 12th standard Physics, Chemistry, and Biology (PCB) textbooks.
  • AIIMS-MBBS (All India Institute of Medical Sciences): This is an entrance exam conducted by the National Board of Examinations (NBE) for admission to the MBBS program at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) in New Delhi and its six other branches. The syllabus for AIIMS-MBBS is similar to NEET, but it is more challenging.
  • JIPMER (Jawaharlal Institute of Postgraduate Medical Education and Research): This is an entrance exam conducted by the NBE for admission to the MBBS program at the Jawaharlal Institute of Postgraduate Medical Education and Research (JIPMER) in Pondicherry. The syllabus for JIPMER is similar to NEET, but it also includes questions on mathematics.

2. What are the eligibility criteria for NEET?

The eligibility criteria for NEET are:

  • Age: 17 years as of December 31st of the year of NEET examination
  • Nationality: Indian citizen or a foreigner with domicile in India
  • Educational qualification: Pass in 12th standard with Physics, Chemistry, and Biology as compulsory subjects

3. What is the syllabus for NEET?

The syllabus for NEET is based on the 11th and 12th standard Physics, Chemistry, and Biology (PCB) textbooks. The following topics are covered in the syllabus:

  • Physics: Mechanics, Electromagnetism, Optics, Modern Physics
  • Chemistry: Atomic structure, Chemical bonding, Chemical reactions, Organic chemistry, Physical chemistry
  • Biology: Cell biology, Genetics, Molecular biology, Ecology, Human physiology

4. What is the difficulty level of NEET?

The difficulty level of NEET is considered to be moderate. The exam is designed to test the basic concepts of Physics, Chemistry, and Biology. However, the exam is competitive and the cut-off scores are high.

5. How can I prepare for NEET?

There are many ways to prepare for NEET. You can start by studying the syllabus thoroughly and solving practice questions. You can also join a coaching institute or take online courses. It is important to start your preparation early and to be consistent with your studies.

6. What are the benefits of cracking NEET?

There are many benefits to cracking NEET. You will be eligible to get admission to any medical college in India. You will also be eligible for scholarships and financial assistance. A career in medicine is a rewarding one and can lead to a good salary and job satisfaction.

7. What are the best study materials for NEET?

There are many study materials available for NEET, but some of the best ones include:

  • NCERT textbooks: The NCERT textbooks are a good starting point for your preparation. They cover the entire syllabus and are written in a clear and concise manner.
  • Practice questions: There are many practice questions available online and in books. Solving these questions will help you to test your knowledge and identify your weak areas.
  • Coaching institutes: There are many coaching institutes that offer NEET preparation courses. These courses can be helpful if you need extra guidance and support.
  • Online courses: There are also many online courses available for NEET preparation. These courses can be convenient and flexible, and they can be a good option if you are unable to attend a coaching institute.

8. What are some tips for staying motivated during NEET preparation?

It can be difficult to stay motivated during NEET preparation, especially when the syllabus is so vast and the competition is so fierce. Here are a few tips to help you stay motivated:

  • Set realistic goals: Don't try to cram the entire syllabus in a few weeks. Set realistic goals for yourself and break down the syllabus into smaller chunks.
  • Reward yourself: When you achieve a goal, reward yourself with something you enjoy. This will help you to stay motivated and on track.
  • Find a study buddy: Studying with a friend or classmate can help you to stay accountable and motivated.
  • Take breaks: Don't try to study for hours on end. Take breaks every 20-30 minutes to avoid burnout.
  • Stay positive: It's important to stay positive and believe in yourself. Remember that you are capable of achieving your goals.

9. What are some common mistakes that NEET aspirants make?

Here are some common mistakes that NEET aspirants make:

  • Not starting their preparation early: It is important to start your preparation early so that you have enough time to cover the entire syllabus.
  • Not solving practice questions: Solving practice questions is essential for testing your knowledge and identifying your weak areas.
  • Not attending a coaching institute: A good coaching institute can provide you with the guidance and support you need to succeed in NEET.
  • Not taking breaks: Studying for hours on end can lead to burnout. It is important to take breaks every 20-30 minutes to avoid burnout.
  • Not staying positive: It is important to stay positive and believe in yourself. Remember that you are capable of achieving your goals.

10. What are some resources that can help me with my NEET preparation?

There are many resources available to help you with your NEET preparation. Here are a few of the most popular ones:

  • The NEET website: The NEET website has a wealth of information, including the syllabus, sample questions, and exam dates.
  • The NEET preparation forum: The NEET preparation forum is a great place to ask questions and get help from other NEET aspirants.
  • The NEET preparation app: There are many NEET preparation apps available that can help you to learn the syllabus and practice questions.
  • The NEET preparation book: There are many NEET preparation books available that can help you to learn the syllabus and practice questions.
